children: U.S. crude oil futures climbed above $105/bbl Tuesday, rising for the 10th time in the past 11 trading sessions, as Saudi Arabia reportedly canceled or deferred shipments to some European refiners that were scheduled to load in late September.

At least three European refiners have seen cargoes at the Yanbu export terminal on the Red Sea canceled or pushed from the final 10 days of this month to as late as November, and all Saudi cargoes scheduled to load in the final 10 days of September are at risk of being canceled, Argus Media reported, citing shipping industry sources.
The delays appear to indicate a prolonged outage at Saudi Aramco's (
) 7M bbl/day East-West crude pipeline, which has been shut since a drone and missile attack on September 10.

The cancellations have strengthened expectations that European refiners will turn to U.S. supplies, helping lift U.S. WTI crude relative to Brent, Lipow Oil Associates president Andy Lipow said in a note.
U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright told CNBC on Tuesday that oil ​should be flowing through the key Saudi pipeline within days, although most analysts have said the outage could last several weeks.

The attacks on oil infrastructure mark a significant escalation of the Middle East conflict ​and increased the probability ⁠of Brent rising above $120/bbl, Goldman Sachs said in a report, citing a scenario in which average Persian Gulf oil output in 2027 remains 4M bbl/day below pre-war levels.

Meanwhile, prices for some physical oil cargoes in Europe jumped above $130/bbl on Tuesday, approaching record highs reached in ‌April, Reuters reported, as buyers rushed to find alternatives to disrupted Middle East supplies.

Some of the factors that have helped cushion the global oil market against supply disruptions are starting to weaken, Commonwealth Bank of Australia's Vivek Dhar said in a note, as China's crude imports are edging higher, while additional non-OPEC+ supply outside the Middle East is unlikely to come online until 2027.
Adding to upward pressure on oil Tuesday was a Reuters reports that Libya's national oil company has suspended operations at two oilfields and a pumping station due to protests.
Nymex diesel prices reached a record high Tuesday, with the front-month October ultra-low sulfur diesel contract (
) surging 6% to $5.262/gal, while front-month Nymex October RBOB gasoline (
) gained 4.4% to $3.4652/gal, its highest close since August 31.
for October jumped 4.4% to $105.83/bbl and front-month Brent crude
for November delivery climbed 2.9% to $108.75/bbl, the highest for both benchmarks since May 19.
